chapter: Le Ruban Bleu, retirement and community work
title: Living in the same house and plans for the House That Jazz Built
summary: She has lived in the neighborhood thirty-five years and plans to involve the kids in the House's activities.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Politics, race and the state of the country

blocks.x: I've been living here in the same house for thirty-five years and I don't feel like I want to go anyplace. I like it here and I got alot of friends here, and some of the community work I've done here. I feel like, well where am I going? It isn't that easy to pick up and go. So that's what I talked about. And then I told them about to what extent I was involved in the community at this particular point, you know, I established The House That Jazz Built a few years ago and it's a project that I'm very much interested in and working with and making some headway. I'm going to be doing some things this year or this winter or up until spring of 1981 through the New York City Youth Board and the Board of Education. We're going to take programs sponsored by The House That Jazz Built into a school, an after-school program. And I'll be working with kids from the age group 7 to 14 and 14 to 19 years old. And our program is geared to meeting improvement through the study of one hundred years of jazz. So I don't, know how much they're going to improve in their reading but they're going to know a whole lot of new terms. But it looks very good. I'm very happy about it and I think we're

going to have a lot of fun. And we intend to involve the kids very much so I think there's a lot of talent in the area and the Bronx seems to be like out of everything. We want them to know the Bronx is here. We have a lot of musicians who live in the Bronx but they take their talents down-town. After all, down-town is the Apple but the Bronx is part of the apple too. Well it is now, we just might pull out any minute and become part of the mainland. We are the only borough that's connected to the mainland. So we might secede. Anyway I moved here in 1945. I liked it because it was residential. It's not that I was very busy working down-town. I - when I moved here I had been all over the City looking for some-place to live, Brooklyn, Long Island, and then I found this house and I'm a half hour at the most down-town on the subway. And it couldn't be anymore convenient. And then it was a wonderful place to raise kids when Paula was a little girl. And so I was lucky. I found this little house.
